items.followUp: Define a saturated solution and identify its solute and solvent.

rubric.why: The solute is the substance that is dissolved.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the solute as the substance dissolved in a solution.

rubric.why: The solvent is the medium that dissolves the solute.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the solvent as the dissolving medium.

modelAnswer: A solute is the substance that is dissolved in a solvent.
A solvent is the medium in which the solute dissolves.

items.followUp: How would you prepare 500 cm³ of a 1 M sodium chloride solution?

rubric.why: A one-molar solution contains one mole of solute per litre of solution.
rubric.description: Specifies the amount of solute for a one-molar solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that one mole (or one gram-molecular mass) of solute is required.

rubric.why: The solution is made up to a final volume of one litre.
rubric.description: Specifies the final volume of solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the solution is made up to 1 L (1000 cm³ or 1 dm³).

modelAnswer: Take one mole (one gram-molecular mass) of the solute and dissolve it in a small amount of solvent.
Add more solvent until the total volume of the solution is 1 litre (1000 cm³).

items.followUp: Define reduction using oxygen and electron-transfer definitions.

rubric.why: Oxidation can be defined as addition of oxygen or loss of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating addition of oxygen or loss of electrons.

rubric.why: Removal of hydrogen or loss of electrons is also an accepted description of oxidation.
rubric.description: Gives a second accepted description of oxidation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating removal of hydrogen or loss of electrons.

modelAnswer: Oxidation is the process in which oxygen is added to a substance or hydrogen is removed from it.
In terms of electrons, oxidation is the loss of electrons by an atom or ion.

items.followUp: What is an oxidizing agent? Give one example.

rubric.why: A reducing agent causes another substance to be reduced, commonly by donating electrons or removing oxygen.
rubric.description: Defines the action of a reducing agent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing how a reducing agent reduces another substance.

rubric.why: A suitable example is hydrogen or carbon reducing copper oxide to copper.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of a reducing agent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a valid reducing agent and the substance it reduces.

modelAnswer: A reducing agent is a substance that causes another substance to be reduced, for example by donating electrons.
Hydrogen is a reducing agent; it reduces copper oxide to copper: H₂ + CuO → Cu + H₂O.

items.followUp: Write two physical properties of copper metal.

rubric.why: Silver is lustrous, malleable, ductile, and conducts heat and electricity well.
rubric.description: States one physical property of silver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct physical property of silver.

rubric.why: A second distinct physical property is required.
rubric.description: States a second physical property of silver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second correct physical property; do not award twice for repeating the same property.

modelAnswer: Silver is malleable and ductile, and it is a good conductor of heat and electricity.

items.followUp: Define valency and write the valency of chlorine.

rubric.why: Valency describes an atom's combining capacity, related to electrons lost, gained, or shared.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining valency as the combining capacity of an atom or through its electron transfer or sharing.
Award 1 mark for stating that sodium's valency is 1.

modelAnswer: Valency is the combining capacity of an atom, determined by the number of electrons it loses, gains, or shares.

items.followUp: Describe the trend in electronegativity across a period of the periodic table.

rubric.why: Electropositivity decreases across a period from left to right.
rubric.description: States the direction of the trend.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electropositivity decreases from left to right across a period.

rubric.why: Increasing nuclear charge makes atoms less likely to lose electrons, so electropositivity decreases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the trend to increasing nuclear charge or reduced tendency to lose electrons.

modelAnswer: Electropositivity decreases from left to right across a period of the periodic table.
This is because nuclear charge increases, so atoms become less likely to lose electrons.

items.followUp: Write two physical properties of gold metal.

rubric.why: Platinum is silvery white, lustrous, malleable, ductile, has a high melting point, and conducts heat and electricity.
rubric.description: States one physical property of platinum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct physical property of platinum.

rubric.why: A second distinct physical property is required.
rubric.description: States a second physical property of platinum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second correct physical property; do not award twice for repeating the same property.

modelAnswer: Platinum is a silvery-white, lustrous metal.
It is malleable and ductile, has a high melting point, and conducts heat and electricity well.
